title: Connection sectors, holonomy and presymplectic boundaries

items.title: Fixed-topology affine sector of normalized circle connections
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth tangent-bundle and principal-connection convention. Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold used for normalized circle-connection data. Fix a smooth right principal $U(1)$ bundle $P\to M$, one countable trivializing cover $(U_i)$ with transition functions $g_{ij}$ in the convention $z_j=g_{ij}^{-1}z_i$, and one normalization constant $\kappa_0>0$ measured in webers. Let $(a_i)$ and $(a_i')$ be two smooth normalized connection representatives for this same atlas, each satisfying $a_j=a_i+\lambda(g_{ij})$ and $a_j'=a_i'+\lambda(g_{ij})$, where $\lambda(g):=-i g^{-1}dg$. In length-coordinate charts, the components of $a_i$ and $a_i'$ have units $\mathrm m^{-1}$; the physical potentials $A_i=\kappa_0a_i$ and $A_i'=\kappa_0a_i'$ have components $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-1}$.

Then $\alpha_i:=a_i'-a_i$ is the restriction of a unique smooth global real one-form $\alpha$ on $M$. The normalized curvatures $f|_{U_i}=da_i$ and $f'|_{U_i}=da_i'$ are global, and $f'-f=d\alpha$. The physical curvatures $F=\kappa_0 f$ and $F'=\kappa_0 f'$ satisfy $F'-F=\kappa_0d\alpha$; in length-coordinate charts their components have units $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-2}$. Consequently $\int_S\iota^*F'=\int_S\iota^*F$ for every compact oriented smooth surface $S$ without boundary and smooth embedding $\iota:S\hookrightarrow M$. The representatives on a fixed bundle and atlas form an affine space over $\Omega^1(M)$.

For a smooth local gauge map $\Phi_h(x,z)=(x,h(x)z)$, the adopted pushforward action on horizontal distributions changes the local representative by $a_i\mapsto a_i-\lambda(h)$; this sign is part of the stated convention.

items.title: Fixed-background Maxwell presymplectic current
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as inherited from the smooth principal-connection convention. Fix an oriented, time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N,o)$ and a fixed normalized $U(1)$ connection sector as in the fixed-topology affine-sector result. Its connection variations are global smooth real one-forms $\alpha,\beta\in\Omega^1(M)$, with components of unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$ in length-coordinate charts. Length-coordinate charts use metre-valued coordinates, with $x^0=ct_{\mathrm{sec}}$ when time is recorded in seconds; $c$ is a coordinate unit-conversion scale in $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$, with no numerical measured value or physical role asserted. Impose the fixed-background Maxwell operator equations $d\star_g d\alpha=0$ and $d\star_g d\beta=0$, where $\star_g$ is the oriented Lorentzian Hodge map of signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Define the real three-form

$$\omega_g(\alpha,\beta):=\alpha\wedge\star_g d\beta-\beta\wedge\star_g d\alpha.$$

Let $\iota_\Sigma:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$ be an oriented smooth embedding of a possibly noncompact three-dimensional manifold, and require the induced metric $\gamma:=\iota_\Sigma^*g$ to be positive definite. Its oriented Riemannian volume form is the nowhere-vanishing three-form $\mathrm{vol}_\gamma$ whose expression in each positively oriented chart $y=(y^1,y^2,y^3)$ is $\sqrt{\det(\gamma_{ij})}\,dy^1\wedge dy^2\wedge dy^3$. Let $\mu_\gamma$ be the positive smooth density measure with coordinate expression $d\mu_\gamma=\sqrt{\det(\gamma_{ij})}\,d^3y$. The density-measure integration supplier listed below gives the chart-independent measure and integral; for a real $L^1(\mu_\gamma)$ function its signed integral is the finite difference of the integrals of its positive and negative parts, and its chart formula is absolutely convergent.

There is a unique smooth real function $u_{\alpha,\beta}$ on $\Sigma$ such that $\iota_\Sigma^*\omega_g(\alpha,\beta)=u_{\alpha,\beta}\,\mathrm{vol}_\gamma$. Define the pairing $\Omega_\Sigma(\alpha,\beta)$ precisely when $u_{\alpha,\beta}\in L^1(\Sigma,\mu_\gamma)$, meaning $\int_\Sigma|u_{\alpha,\beta}|\,d\mu_\gamma<\infty$, and then set $\Omega_\Sigma(\alpha,\beta):=\int_\Sigma u_{\alpha,\beta}\,d\mu_\gamma$. This absolute-integrability condition is the convergence convention on noncompact $\Sigma$ and makes the value independent of any exhaustion or ordering. In length coordinates on $\Sigma$, the coefficients of $d\alpha$ and $d\beta$ have units $\mathrm m^{-2}$, those of $\omega_g$ have units $\mathrm m^{-3}$, $u_{\alpha,\beta}$ has units $\mathrm m^{-3}$, and $d\mu_\gamma$ has volume units $\mathrm m^3$; thus the normalized integral is dimensionless. Replacing normalized variations by physical-potential variations $\kappa_0\alpha$ and $\kappa_0\beta$ multiplies the current by $\kappa_0^2$; an action prefactor is not fixed here.

This is a mathematical fixed-metric Maxwell-block definition. The equations are imposed on the normalized connection variations. The item does not identify $\kappa_0d\alpha$ with the geometric-normalized electrovac field of the coupled Einstein–Maxwell equations, prescribe a conversion between those normalizations, include metric variations, or claim to define the full coupled covariant phase-space current.

items.title: Closed Maxwell current and gauge boundary term
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $g$ be a fixed oriented Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on a smooth four-manifold, and let $\alpha,\beta\in\Omega^1(M)$ be smooth normalized connection variations satisfying $d\star_g d\alpha=d\star_g d\beta=0$. For $\omega_g(\alpha,\beta)=\alpha\wedge\star_g d\beta-\beta\wedge\star_g d\alpha$, one has $d\omega_g(\alpha,\beta)=0$. For every smooth real function $\chi$ on $M$, replacing $\alpha$ by $\alpha+d\chi$ changes the current by $d(\chi\star_g d\beta)$. Hence, for every finite smooth singular three-chain $c$, the integrated change is $\int_{\partial c}\chi\star_g d\beta$; it vanishes when $c$ is a cycle.

For a noncompact oriented spacelike hypersurface $\iota_\Sigma:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$, suppose both $\Omega_\Sigma(\alpha,\beta)$ and $\Omega_\Sigma(\alpha+d\chi,\beta)$ are defined by the absolute-integrability convention of the preceding presymplectic-current definition. Write $\iota_\Sigma^*(\omega_g(\alpha+d\chi,\beta)-\omega_g(\alpha,\beta))=u\,\mathrm{vol}_\gamma$. For every compact Borel exhaustion $K_n\subseteq K_{n+1}$ with $\bigcup_nK_n=\Sigma$, one has $\int_{K_n}u\,d\mu_\gamma\to\int_\Sigma u\,d\mu_\gamma$. If the exhaustion has finite smooth singular three-chains $c_n$ supported in $K_n$ satisfying $\int_{c_n}\tau=\int_{K_n}u_\tau\,d\mu_\gamma$ for every smooth three-form $\tau=u_\tau\,\mathrm{vol}_\gamma$ on $\Sigma$, using the induced metric and density fixed in that definition, then

$$\Omega_\Sigma(\alpha+d\chi,\beta)-\Omega_\Sigma(\alpha,\beta)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_{\partial c_n}\chi\star_g d\beta.$$

The limit exists and is independent of the compact exhaustion and its smooth-chain representatives. For a fixed $\beta$, the pairing shift vanishes exactly when this limiting boundary flux is zero. Given any linear subspace $\mathcal V$ of smooth real one-form solutions $\beta$ of $d\star_g d\beta=0$ for which both pairings are defined, call the exact gauge direction $d\chi$ degenerate on $\mathcal V$ when its pairing shift vanishes for every $\beta\in\mathcal V$. Thus degeneracy on $\mathcal V$ holds exactly when this limit vanishes for every $\beta\in\mathcal V$.

items.title: Finite constrained mode quotient
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space with a nondegenerate alternating bilinear form $\\omega:V\\times V\\to\\mathbb R$. For a linear subspace $W\\subseteq V$, define $W^\\omega:=\\{v\\in V:\\omega(v,w)=0\\text{ for every }w\\in W\\}$, and assume $W^\\omega\\subseteq W$ (so $W$ is coisotropic). Then the quotient vector space $W/W^\\omega$, whose elements are cosets $[u]:=u+W^\\omega$, carries the well-defined symplectic form $\\overline\\omega([u],[v])=\\omega(u,v)$. This proposition concerns only finite-dimensional constrained mode models; it does not assert that an infinite-dimensional Einstein–Maxwell solution space has a smooth symplectic quotient.

items.title: Flat circle connection: holonomy and gauge triviality
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth principal-connection and gauge-action convention. Let $M_0=\mathbb R_{x^0}	imes U(1)_w	imes\mathbb R^2_{x,y}$ have the product smooth structure and flat Lorentzian metric $g=-(dx^0)^2+R^2d\phi^2+dx^2+dy^2$, where $x^0,x,y$ are length coordinates measured in metres, $R>0$ is a length, and $\phi$ is dimensionless modulo $2\pi$. On each angular chart, $s=R\phi$ is a length coordinate and $g=-(dx^0)^2+ds^2+dx^2+dy^2$, so all four coordinates in this chart are metre-valued. In the adopted Lorentzian length-coordinate convention, write $x^0=ct_{\mathrm{sec}}$, where $t_{\mathrm{sec}}$ is measured in seconds and $c>0$ is only a coordinate unit-conversion scale in $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$; no numerical measured value or physical role for $c$ is asserted. Give $M_0$ time orientation $\partial_{x^0}$ and product orientation $dx^0\wedge R
u\wedge dx\wedge dy$. Let $
u=-iw^{-1}dw=d\phi$ be the global real angular one-form on the base circle, normalized by $\int_{U(1)}
u=2\pi$, and let $P=M_0	imes U(1)_z$ have projection $\pi(x,z)=x$ and right action $(x,z)\cdot\zeta=(x,z\zeta)$. On the fibre let $\eta=-iz^{-1}dz$. For a dimensionless real parameter $	heta$, the normalized connection $\omega_	heta=\eta+	heta\pi^*
u$ has zero curvature. For the fixed normalization $\kappa_0>0$ in webers, its physical local potential is $A_	heta=\kappa_0	heta
u$; in the length coordinate $s$ its component is $\kappa_0	heta/R$ in $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-1}$. For the positive base loop $\gamma(\phi)=(0,e^{i\phi},0,0)$, $\phi\in[0,2\pi]$, define principal holonomy as the fibre multiplier of the horizontal lift; it is $e^{-2\pi i	heta}$. The inverse Wilson-loop convention $W(\gamma):=\exp(i\int_\gamma	heta
u)$ gives $e^{2\pi i	heta}$. Under the pushforward action on horizontal distributions, this connection is gauge-equivalent to $\eta$ exactly when $	heta\in\mathbb Z$. The circle is an ideal topological factor of a smooth background; no monopole, charge quantization, or empirical claim is made.
